result.title: Controlling the Humanoid Robot H1-2 With a Simulated Biologically Plausible Network
result.summary: Artificial Spiking Neural Networks have gained remarkable attention in the last few years due to their proven ability in simulating biological neural cultures and producing similar activity and trends. Nevertheless, whether they can be trained for humanoid locomotion while retaining biological plausibility and robust performance at once remains an open question. We study this problem by proposing a biologically inspired spiking network, trained by different learning schemes and tested on the H1-2 Unitree Humanoid. These schemes differ in how recurrent weights are trained. Ordered from most to least biologically faithful, they are: a fixed reservoir mimicking an in-vitro neural culture, where recurrent weights are kept frozen and only a linear readout is trained, the same network but with its synapses trained by reward-modulated spike timing dependent plasticity and eligibility propagation, and finally backpropagation through time as a non biological baseline for comparison. All schemes relied on distillation of a reinforcement learning expert policy with dataset aggregation. We show that e-prop reached 100% survival rate matching backpropagation through time, whereas both the fixed reservoir and the reward-modulated STDP, though the closest to biological cultures, plateaued at a much lower performance (~43.7% and ~11% survival). We explore in further detail which trends a real culture could and could not produce until now. Finally we demonstrate brief bipedal stepping on a full size humanoid H1-2.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作构建生物启发的脉冲神经网络控制 Unitree H1-2 人形机器人行走，通过蒸馏 RL 专家策略，并比较三种循环权重训练方案（冻结储层加线性读出、奖励调制 STDP 与 e-prop、BPTT）的存活率表现。
AI.relevance_reason: e-prop 的资格迹式跨时间信用分配，以及「冻结随机循环动力学、仅训练读出」与训练循环权重的对照，可能为 LVR 中 latent 轨迹的监督信号分配和多步循环状态更新提供可核查的训练线索；但任务是机器人运动控制，缺少视觉证据与推理期评价，相关性需自行判断。
